oliver: Running into a weird one999999999999ruby sampleapp OIDC flow fails with upstream 400.
jen: Any raw request or stacktrace?
oliver: App log shows: 
```
Net::HTTPBadResponse: wrong status line: "GET /v1/..."
```
kai: That points to a mangled request. Can you paste the captured request headers?
oliver: The Authorization header is truncated about 2k in; token is ~3.1k chars. If I bypass our local ingress proxy and hit backend directly, everything is fine.
nina: Could be proxy header limits, or a stray control char in the header value causing folding.
kai: Our Go sample trims token before setting header (`strings.TrimSpace`) so it never had this issue. Do we do the same in Ruby?
oliver: Not in the connector. Found this line: `headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{token}\n"` 99999999999999999999999`
nina: Trailing newline explains it. Some proxies (or header parsers) treat that as folded header and drop remainder.
jen: Fix plan: sanitize token when building headers (e.g., `token.gsub(/[\r\n\s]+/, '')` or at least `token.strip`). Add unit that constructs headers and asserts no control chars.
kai: Also add a Quickstart troubleshooting snippet: "If auth headers look truncated, check SDK helpers for stray control chars and verify your ingress header limits." Keep parity with Go SDK which already trims.
oliver: I'll open a small PR: trim token, add unit test, update Quickstart.
ci-bot: CI kicked: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/4567 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ci-bot: CI passed: https://ci.redwood/sampleapp/4567 :white_check_mark:
jen: Also add a short entry in the SDK migration notes about long OIDC JWTs and proxies, so support articles can link to it.
kai: Good idea 9999999999999999999999
oliver: Thanks all, will validate against corp ingress tomorrow and report back. :thumbsup:
